Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships
San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA

About Anthropic

Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As the Manager of the Partnerships Applied AI Solutions Architect team, you will drive adoption of frontier AI by enabling deployment of Anthropic's products (Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, API) through our Global and Regional System Integrators, cloud partners (AWS, GCP, Azure), and strategic technology partners.

You will build and lead a team of Partner Solutions Architects, establish processes and best practices for partner-led pre-sales engagements, and represent Anthropic as the technical lead on its most important partnerships. In collaboration with Sales, Partnerships, Product, and Engineering, you will help partners incorporate leading-edge AI into their practices, accelerate indirect revenue, and execute long-term GTM strategy while maintaining our best-in-class safety standards.

Responsibilities

    Team Leadership & Development: Hire, manage, and mentor a team of Partner Solutions Architects. Set goals, run reviews, and coach each team member toward high productivity and career growth.
    Strategic Technical Partnership: Act as the senior technical thought partner to Anthropic's GTM partnerships team. Co-build partner strategy with aligned GTM leadership, drive key programs, and align cross-functional stakeholders (Sales, Product, Engineering) behind partner outcomes.
    Partner Enablement & Ecosystem: Embed your team with GSI and cloud partner technical teams to enable their AI practices, troubleshoot, and evangelize Anthropic in their developer communities. Represent Anthropic at partner events (GSI workshops, AWS/GCP summits, hackathons) and contribute technical content and thought leadership.
    Joint Solution Development: Lead partners in identifying high-value, industry-specific GenAI applications. Develop joint solutions and codify reference architectures and best practices to accelerate time to deployment.
    Customer Deal Support: Own the technical portion of partner-led pre-sales engagements. Intervene directly on strategic deals where partners are the primary delivery vehicle, providing deep solution architecture guidance.
    Product Feedback: Gather and validate feedback on Anthropic's products from partner deployments and deliver it to Product and Engineering to inform roadmap and partner strategy.

You may be a good fit if you have

    7+ years in technical customer-facing or partner-facing roles (Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Partner SE, TAM).
    3+ years managing pre-sales or partner-facing technical teams; comfortable building foundational teams in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.
    Track record building and scaling partnerships with GSIs (e.g., Accenture, Deloitte, TCS, Infosys) and/or cloud providers (AWS, GCP, Azure).
    Deep understanding of partner-led selling and delivery: indirect revenue models, enablement at scale, and joint GTM motions.
    Technical depth in enterprise AI deployments: LLM architecture, prompt engineering, evaluation, API integrations, and production use cases.
    Exceptional communication and executive presence; able to build trusted relationships with C-suite, partner leadership, and engineering teams alike.
    A love of teaching and mentoring, and a passion for advancing safe, beneficial AI.

Strong candidates may also have

    5+ years leading partner-facing SA teams through hypergrowth, including developing both senior and junior talent.
    Direct experience helping GSIs or consultancies build their AI/ML practice - enablement programs, certification paths, joint solution development.

Compensation

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role's On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary: $315,000 - $380,000 USD

# Anthropic - Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships briefing packet
| Manager of Applied AI Architecture, Partnerships | $315,000–$380,000 USD OTE | Reports to Partnerships (specific reporting line not verified) |

## JD Complement
Anthropic’s partnership opportunity is to help external delivery organizations turn Claude capabilities into consistent enterprise outcomes. The challenge is not access to a model alone; it is creating confidence that customers can adopt,
govern, and expand AI use without fragmented implementation quality.

This position sits at the intersection of commercial scale and technical stewardship. Services firms, cloud providers, and technology partners can extend reach into large accounts, yet their delivery approaches must align with Anthropic’s
expectations for trustworthy, secure, and useful AI.

The likely mandate is to create a durable operating system for partner technical work: qualification criteria, reusable solution patterns, practical enablement, clear escalation routes, and structured learning from the field.

## Company DNA & Operating Model
Anthropic presents itself as an AI safety and research company focused on systems that are reliable, interpretable, and steerable. That identity makes deployment quality a strategic concern rather than a purely post-sale concern.

The company combines frontier-model development with products for individual users, enterprise organizations, and developers. Claude is available through enterprise experiences and programmatic interfaces, allowing customers to use it
within both employee workflows and custom software.

Anthropic is not primarily a professional-services business. Its ecosystem must therefore expand implementation capacity while preserving a coherent product experience and avoiding excessive dependence on one-off delivery work.

A strong partner architecture function can help define where standardization is essential, where partner flexibility is valuable, and how customer requirements should influence product priorities.

## Company Strategy & Operating Pressure
Claude is positioned for analytical work, writing, coding, data-oriented tasks, and complex problem solving. Broad applicability increases addressable demand, but it can also create diffuse evaluations and generic use cases that do not
advance beyond experimentation.

Enterprise adoption requires a bridge between technical configuration and organizational behavior. Anthropic’s deployment materials address setup, launch, change management, and continued adoption, indicating that successful use depends
on more than selecting a capable model.

The strategic need is likely to make high-value use cases easier to identify, validate, deploy, and repeat. Partners can contribute industry context and delivery capacity, while Anthropic provides product expertise and deployment
guardrails.

As enterprise usage grows, the company must distinguish platform limitations from delivery gaps, customer readiness issues, and unclear solution design. A disciplined field-feedback process is critical to making those distinctions.

## Leadership & Stakeholder Map
The supplied research does not confirm a named manager or formal reporting chain. The effective stakeholder environment is likely cross-functional and organized around shared customer and partner outcomes.

- Product and Engineering teams need synthesized evidence from deployments, not isolated requests or anecdotal field escalation.

## AI, Data, Platform, Architecture Signals
Anthropic’s stated focus on trustworthy AI makes architecture inseparable from control, explainability, adoption readiness, and business fit. The relevant conversation extends beyond model selection to how customers use AI responsibly
inside real operating environments.

Claude spans user-facing enterprise workflows and developer-oriented integration paths. Effective partner guidance should connect these paths rather than treating enterprise workspace adoption and application development as unrelated
motions.

Enterprise offerings emphasize security, compliance, and support for organizational users and builders. Useful architecture patterns will likely address identity, administration, workflow design, evaluation approaches, rollout sequencing,
and operational ownership.

Claude’s positioning around coding, analysis, and problem solving creates an opening for solution patterns tied to measurable workflows. The strongest partner architectures will avoid broad “AI assistant” framing in favor of defined user
needs, implementation constraints, and success measures.

Because change management appears in Anthropic’s adoption guidance, technical credibility in this role should include how teams move from initial access to sustained usage. Architecture should account for users, process owners, security
teams, and delivery partners—not only interfaces and integrations.

## Partnership / Ecosystem Motion
Anthropic publicly presents a network of cloud, technology, and services partners as part of its path to solving enterprise AI challenges. This points to an ecosystem strategy in which partners provide customer proximity, domain context,
implementation capacity, and routes into established technology environments.

Systems integrators can be particularly important because they influence transformation programs and can spread technical practices across many engagements. Their value grows when they can independently deliver high-quality work while
remaining connected to Anthropic’s product and safety expectations.

Accenture’s public positioning of its Anthropic relationship centers on enterprise deployment, productivity, value creation, and creation of new products. This supports the view that implementation partners are expected to help customers
move from interest to operational use.

The core ecosystem question is repeatability. Valuable shared assets may include technical qualification methods, reference designs, deployment playbooks, learning paths, validated industry workflows, and escalation agreements.

Partner scale is not automatically a commercial advantage. It must be accompanied by consistent customer guidance, transparent roles between direct and partner teams, and feedback channels that improve both partner readiness and product
decisions.

## Recent Events & Urgency
Anthropic’s public partner presence and enterprise-adoption resources suggest that scaling implementation capability is increasingly important to its commercial model. The company is building visible infrastructure around both
ecosystem participation and organizational rollout.

Enterprise AI adoption involves multiple entry points: business users seeking immediate productivity, developer teams embedding capabilities in applications, and administrators responsible for policy and access. These constituencies may
engage through different partners but require a connected experience.

The need for structured partner enablement is heightened by the pace of enterprise AI competition. Model quality matters, but customers also assess how quickly they can identify practical use cases, implement safely, and demonstrate
value.

Anthropic has an opportunity to differentiate through delivery consistency. A strong partner technical organization can make safety-oriented product principles tangible in customer environments while reducing friction in the path from
evaluation to scaled use.

## apps_rg Positioning Themes (targeting only, not proof)
- Establishing scalable enablement for consulting, cloud, and technology alliances.
- Translating AI platform capabilities into reusable enterprise solution patterns.

## apps_lic Outreach Angles (targeting only, not proof)
- Services partners can provide reach into complex enterprise programs, but only if technical practices are made repeatable.
